stories.title: Amazon data center could be tied to the country's most polluting power plant
stories.summary: The Verge reports that a power plant supplying an Amazon data center could become the most polluting power plant in the United States. The report ties into the broader surge in electricity demand from AI data centers, which is pushing utilities toward higher-emission generation to keep up. Details on the specific plant, fuel source, and location were not fully specified in the initial report.
stories.whyItMatters: AI infrastructure's energy appetite is increasingly colliding with climate goals, and a case study this stark could intensify pressure on Amazon and other cloud giants to justify their power sourcing.
whatToWatch: Amazon's response to the reporting
Any regulatory or permitting scrutiny of the plant
Whether other data center operators face similar scrutiny
questions: What fuel source makes this plant so polluting?
Is Amazon contractually committed to this power source long-term?

sources.title: An Amazon data center could have the worst polluting power plant in the country

stories.title: A $450 laptop from an unknown brand raises a 'too good to be true' question

stories.whyItMatters: Unbranded and lesser-known manufacturers undercutting big PC makers on price raises broader questions about supply-chain sourcing, quality control, and after-sale support in the budget laptop market.

stories.title: Mars' first self-driving vehicle proves a smashing success
stories.summary: Ars Technica reports that the first self-driving vehicle deployed on Mars has performed successfully in early operation. The report frames this as a notable win for autonomous navigation technology operating in one of the most extreme, remote environments possible.
stories.whyItMatters: Autonomous navigation software proven in Mars' harsh, communication-delayed conditions can inform terrestrial self-driving and robotics development back on Earth.
whatToWatch: Follow-up mission updates on the vehicle's continued performance
Whether autonomy is expanded to more of its operations
questions: How much human oversight from mission control is still required?

stories.title: X scraps 'misaligned' creator revenue-sharing program for new Original Content Rewards
stories.summary: X is shutting down its existing revenue-sharing program for creators, which it described as misaligned with its goals, and replacing it with a new system called Original Content Rewards, according to TechCrunch. The move changes how creators and publishers get paid for content on the platform.
stories.whyItMatters: Creator monetization is a key lever in X's competition with rival platforms for engagement and talent, and any change to payout mechanics can reshape what content gets made and promoted on the platform.
whatToWatch: Details of how Original Content Rewards calculates payouts
Reaction from creators currently monetizing on X
Whether payouts rise or fall for typical accounts
questions: What specifically was 'misaligned' about the old program?
Will the new system favor different types of content than before?

stories.title: Amazon's Kindle Scribe Colorsoft brings color e-ink to its writable tablet line

stories.whyItMatters: Amazon extending color e-ink into its Scribe line signals where it sees the next competitive front in e-reader hardware, against rivals like Kobo and reMarkable.

stories.title: Census proposal would drop counts of undocumented immigrants, race, and sexual orientation
stories.summary: Wired reports on a proposal that would change how the Census counts the population, stopping the counting of undocumented immigrants and dropping race and sexual orientation as tracked categories. The report does not detail the proposal's current procedural status.
stories.whyItMatters: Census data underpins demographic research, market analysis, and ad targeting used broadly across the tech and data industries, so changes to what's counted ripple well beyond government.
whatToWatch: Whether the proposal advances through any formal rulemaking or legislative process
Response from advocacy groups and data researchers
questions: What is the stated rationale for dropping these categories?

stories.title: Trump administration's offshore wind war has cost nearly $4 billion — and it may be losing
stories.summary: The Trump administration has spent close to $4 billion on efforts to cancel offshore wind farm projects, including another $1.2 billion in a recent round, according to TechCrunch and Engadget. Despite that spending, Ars Technica reports the broader campaign against wind power is faltering.
stories.whyItMatters: Offshore wind is part of the power mix that utilities and tech companies are counting on to meet surging electricity demand from data centers, so sustained policy uncertainty here affects long-term energy planning across the industry.
whatToWatch: Whether additional offshore wind projects face cancellation attempts
Legal challenges from developers or states
Any court rulings on the administration's authority to block projects
questions: Which specific offshore wind projects remain at risk?
How are affected developers and utilities adjusting their plans?
